interpretations.explanation: ECG of 3/7/2026, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of 81/min (RR 656-856 ms, gradual slowing typical of sinus arrhythmia); an upright P wave of about 0.18 mV precedes every QRS in lead II with a constant PR of 184 ms. QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +48 degrees (normal). QT 327 ms, Bazett QTc 379 ms - normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. No prior ECG for comparison. This confirms the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

ECG of 7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR 568-586 ms), upright P waves in II (0.18 mV) with a PR of 128 ms - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal AF is documented in the notes. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +37 degrees (normal). QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 486 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 6/20/2025 (100698634: sinus tachycardia 147/min, PR 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 432 ms) the rate has slowed; the QTc rose by about 54 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold, and rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

ECG of 5/21/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus tachycardia at 110/min, regular (RR 540-614 ms), with upright P waves in II before each QRS and a PR of 118 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 342 ms; Bazett QTc 462 ms, mildly prolonged largely because of rate correction at this heart rate. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: mean rate 144/min with irregularly irregular RR intervals from 348 to 650 ms (CV 0.16, RMSSD 98 ms), no consistent P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.41) and therefore no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +1 degree (normal). QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 440 ms. The prior tracing from earlier the same day (107914094, 17:13) showed the same rhythm at 139/min with QTc 436 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note recorded this study as normal sinus rhythm at 72/min, which is contradicted by both tracings.

ECG of 8/2/2025. Sinus rhythm at 69/min, very regular (RR 864-884 ms), with repeatable atrial activity before every QRS and a PR of 148 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal, with a leftward tendency: lead I strongly positive, aVL positive, III negative). QT 408 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 (104232242) shows sinus rhythm at 60/min with QTc 408 ms but with reversed arm leads (negative P and QRS in lead I, positive QRS in aVR, normal precordial progression), which accounts for its apparently extreme axis. No change in rhythm or conduction, and the QTc difference of 29 ms is below the 60 ms threshold.

ECG of 5/23/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 596-630 ms), with upright P waves in II (0.17 mV) and a PR of 104 ms. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +4 degrees (normal). QT 306 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, very regular (RR 494-504 ms), with consistent upright P waves in II and a PR of 142 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +52 degrees (normal). QT 274 ms, QTc 389 ms (Bazett). Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (106186980: sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 396 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc - only a slightly faster rate.

ECG of 10/8/2023. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with upright P waves in II and a PR of 128 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +47 degrees (normal). The T wave is broad and late: QT 503 ms with a Bazett QTc of 536 ms, markedly prolonged. Compared with the prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (100065910: sinus 75/min, QTc 359 ms) the QTc has risen by about 177 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged. Escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug, is current - see the QT safety review item.

ECG of 4/19/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular (RR 492-500 ms), upright P in II with PR 130 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +68 degrees (normal). QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 403 ms - normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular, with upright P waves in II and a PR of 140 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +58 degrees (normal). QT 318 ms, QTc 413 ms. The prior tracing (102910502) was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 100/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 407 ms), so there are no interval changes.

ECG of 10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), with a low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave in II before every QRS and a PR of 168 ms - no AV block on this tracing despite the coded history of Mobitz II block, and no atrial fibrillation despite the AF history. QRS 88 ms with prominent voltage (V6 R 3.3 mV) but no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 433 ms, Bazett QTc 402 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/22/2023 (104629882: sinus 58/min with one atrial ectopic beat, QTc 371 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

ECG of 12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, extremely regular (RR 492-496 ms), with a small upright P wave in II and a PR of 126 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms. Low-amplitude limb-lead complexes with a net negative QRS in lead I and net positive aVF give a frontal axis of about +143 degrees, i.e. right axis deviation (the axis is close to indeterminate given the small voltages). QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. The prior ECG from the same day at 01:33 (106516875) showed a QRS of 148 ms with a tall terminal R wave in V1 and wide S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - which has resolved on this tracing, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK applies. QTc fell by 55 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

ECG of 11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular (RR 944-982 ms), with a consistent upright P wave in II and a PR of 168 ms. QRS 96 ms - no bundle branch block; axis +67 degrees (normal). QT 550 ms with a Bazett QTc of 559 ms, markedly prolonged. Compared with the prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (108780865: sinus bradycardia 47/min with one atrial ectopic beat, PR 182 ms, QTc 410 ms) the QTc has increased by about 149 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged. Amiodarone was started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit, two weeks before this tracing - see the QT safety review item.

ECG of 9/17/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular with RR intervals from 386 to 1092 ms (coefficient of variation 0.30, RMSSD 264 ms), no organised P waves are seen and the pre-QRS segments do not repeat from beat to beat (beat-to-beat correlation 0.37), so no PR interval is measurable. Mean ventricular rate 99/min. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -53 degrees, left axis deviation. QT 332 ms with a Bazett QTc of 426 ms using the median RR. No prior ECG for comparison; this tracing documents the atrial fibrillation for which the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +48 degrees (normal). QT 327 ms, Bazett QTc 379 ms - normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. No prior ECG for comparison. This confirms the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

ECG of 7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR 568-586 ms), upright P waves in II (0.18 mV) with a PR of 128 ms - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal AF is documented in the notes. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +37 degrees (normal). QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 486 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms. ECG of 5/21/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus tachycardia at 110/min, regular (RR 540-614 ms), with upright P waves in II before each QRS and a PR of 118 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 342 ms; Bazett QTc 462 ms, mildly prolonged largely because of rate correction at this heart rate. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: mean rate 144/min with irregularly irregular RR intervals from 348 to 650 ms (CV 0.16, RMSSD 98 ms), no consistent P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.41) and therefore no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +1 degree (normal). QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 440 ms. The prior tracing from earlier the same day (107914094, 17:13) showed the same rhythm at 139/min with QTc 436 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note recorded this study as normal sinus rhythm at 72/min, which is contradicted by both tracings.

ECG of 8/2/2025. Sinus rhythm at 69/min, very regular (RR 864-884 ms), with repeatable atrial activity before every QRS and a PR of 148 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal, with a leftward tendency: lead I strongly positive, aVL positive, III negative). QT 408 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 (104232242) shows sinus rhythm at 60/min with QTc 408 ms but with reversed arm leads (negative P and QRS in lead I, positive QRS in aVR, normal precordial progression), which accounts for its apparently extreme axis. No change in rhythm or conduction, and the QTc difference of 29 ms is below the 60 ms threshold.

Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (106186980: sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 396 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc - only a slightly faster rate.

Compared with the prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (100065910: sinus 75/min, QTc 359 ms) the QTc has risen by about 177 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged. Escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug, is current - see the QT safety review item.

Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026 (observation 4282f19b), 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

The anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 documents a home INR of 3.4 and a warfarin decrease from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the clinic protocol - a dose change by a clinic pharmacist, which the 3/1/2026 memo covers. A follow-up INR was therefore required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since the change (the last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; the 3.4 value is the pre-change home reading that prompted it), so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (6/10/2026 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of 139/min with no consistent P waves, and 103088543 (6/10/2026 19:36) shows the same pattern at 144/min (RR intervals 348-650 ms, beat-to-beat P-wave correlation 0.41). Both are atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the tachycardia needs review.

This 80-year-old woman (born 10/26/1945) has no anticoagulant on her current medication list or among her active prescriptions - only aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: age >=75 (2), female (1), hypertension (1), type 2 diabetes (1), congestive heart failure / hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (1), vascular disease - old MI and coronary atherosclerosis (1), and prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria, dysphagia and hemiparesis (2). Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation (class 1) at this risk level; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Anticoagulation needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

Atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 427.31, condition 7010d0e5, 8/22/2025) is an active problem and is restated in the cardiology clinic notes, most recently 6/27/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (1), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery (1). A score of >=2 in a man carries a class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Note the chart also records hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025), so any decision to withhold anticoagulation should be documented explicitly after review.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0, condition 66dd1300) was diagnosed on 3/14/2025 during an admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism of a cerebral artery - i.e. a cardioembolic stroke. This 71-year-old woman (born 9/7/1955) has no anticoagulant current: her active prescriptions are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: age 65-74 (1), female (1), hypertension (1), prior stroke (2). Anticoagulation is a class 1 recommendation, and is particularly compelling for secondary prevention after an embolic stroke with documented AF. The 3/14/2025 ECG (102298909) showed sinus rhythm with a single ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

interpretations.explanation: ECG of 3/7/2026, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of 81/min (RR 656-856 ms, gradual slowing typical of sinus arrhythmia); an upright P wave of about 0.18 mV precedes every QRS in lead II with a constant PR of 184 ms. QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +48 degrees (normal). QT 327 ms, Bazett QTc 379 ms - normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. No prior ECG for comparison. This confirms the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

ECG of 7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR 568-586 ms), upright P waves in II (0.18 mV) with a PR of 128 ms - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal AF is documented in the notes. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +37 degrees (normal). QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 486 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 6/20/2025 (100698634: sinus tachycardia 147/min, PR 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 432 ms) the rate has slowed; the QTc rose by about 54 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold, and rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

ECG of 5/21/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus tachycardia at 110/min, regular (RR 540-614 ms), with upright P waves in II before each QRS and a PR of 118 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 342 ms; Bazett QTc 462 ms, mildly prolonged largely because of rate correction at this heart rate. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: mean rate 144/min with irregularly irregular RR intervals from 348 to 650 ms (CV 0.16, RMSSD 98 ms), no consistent P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.41) and therefore no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +1 degree (normal). QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 440 ms. The prior tracing from earlier the same day (107914094, 17:13) showed the same rhythm at 139/min with QTc 436 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note recorded this study as normal sinus rhythm at 72/min, which is contradicted by both tracings.

ECG of 8/2/2025. Sinus rhythm at 69/min, very regular (RR 864-884 ms), with repeatable atrial activity before every QRS and a PR of 148 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal, with a leftward tendency: lead I strongly positive, aVL positive, III negative). QT 408 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 (104232242) shows sinus rhythm at 60/min with QTc 408 ms but with reversed arm leads (negative P and QRS in lead I, positive QRS in aVR, normal precordial progression), which accounts for its apparently extreme axis. No change in rhythm or conduction, and the QTc difference of 29 ms is below the 60 ms threshold.

ECG of 5/23/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 596-630 ms), with upright P waves in II (0.17 mV) and a PR of 104 ms. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +4 degrees (normal). QT 306 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 12/25/2025, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR 820-840 ms), with a consistent upright P wave in II and a PR of 138 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +22 degrees (normal). QT 381 ms, Bazett QTc 418 ms - normal. No prior ECG for comparison. This tracing predates the escitalopram started on 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

ECG of 11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response: mean rate 53/min with markedly irregular RR intervals from 694 to 1164 ms (CV 0.20, RMSSD 288 ms), no organised P waves and no reproducible pre-QRS atrial activity (beat-to-beat correlation 0.22), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +27 degrees (normal). QT 461 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms using the median RR. The prior ECG of 11/12/2024 (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear 0.22 mV P waves, PR 168 ms and QTc 401 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF); the QTc change of about 33 ms is below the 60 ms threshold.

ECG of 1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, very regular (RR 494-504 ms), with consistent upright P waves in II and a PR of 142 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +52 degrees (normal). QT 274 ms, QTc 389 ms (Bazett). Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (106186980: sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 396 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc - only a slightly faster rate.

ECG of 10/8/2023. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with upright P waves in II and a PR of 128 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +47 degrees (normal). The T wave is broad and late: QT 503 ms with a Bazett QTc of 536 ms, markedly prolonged. Compared with the prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (100065910: sinus 75/min, QTc 359 ms) the QTc has risen by about 177 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged. Escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug, is current - see the QT safety review item.

ECG of 4/19/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular (RR 492-500 ms), upright P in II with PR 130 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +68 degrees (normal). QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 403 ms - normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular, with upright P waves in II and a PR of 140 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +58 degrees (normal). QT 318 ms, QTc 413 ms. The prior tracing (102910502) was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 100/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 407 ms), so there are no interval changes.

ECG of 10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), with a low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave in II before every QRS and a PR of 168 ms - no AV block on this tracing despite the coded history of Mobitz II block, and no atrial fibrillation despite the AF history. QRS 88 ms with prominent voltage (V6 R 3.3 mV) but no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 433 ms, Bazett QTc 402 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/22/2023 (104629882: sinus 58/min with one atrial ectopic beat, QTc 371 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

ECG of 12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, extremely regular (RR 492-496 ms), with a small upright P wave in II and a PR of 126 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms. Low-amplitude limb-lead complexes with a net negative QRS in lead I and net positive aVF give a frontal axis of about +143 degrees, i.e. right axis deviation (the axis is close to indeterminate given the small voltages). QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. The prior ECG from the same day at 01:33 (106516875) showed a QRS of 148 ms with a tall terminal R wave in V1 and wide S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - which has resolved on this tracing, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK applies. QTc fell by 55 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

ECG of 11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular (RR 944-982 ms), with a consistent upright P wave in II and a PR of 168 ms. QRS 96 ms - no bundle branch block; axis +67 degrees (normal). QT 550 ms with a Bazett QTc of 559 ms, markedly prolonged. Compared with the prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (108780865: sinus bradycardia 47/min with one atrial ectopic beat, PR 182 ms, QTc 410 ms) the QTc has increased by about 149 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged. Amiodarone was started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit, two weeks before this tracing - see the QT safety review item.

ECG of 9/17/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular with RR intervals from 386 to 1092 ms (coefficient of variation 0.30, RMSSD 264 ms), no organised P waves are seen and the pre-QRS segments do not repeat from beat to beat (beat-to-beat correlation 0.37), so no PR interval is measurable. Mean ventricular rate 99/min. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -53 degrees, left axis deviation. QT 332 ms with a Bazett QTc of 426 ms using the median RR. No prior ECG for comparison; this tracing documents the atrial fibrillation for which the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

items.explanation: Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban, but both prescriptions were written that day and both remain current at 9/24/2026: rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order c4b6df94, valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7c496afb, valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026). The visit note lists both on the current medication list. Concurrent DOAC therapy markedly increases bleeding risk (this patient also takes clopidogrel) and the rivaroxaban order should be discontinued.

The dose also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised for patients over 60. The most recent ECG, 104821039 of 11/10/2023, shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 505 ms and Bazett QTc 545 ms, above the 500 ms threshold and 101 ms longer than the QTc of 444 ms on the prior ECG of 6/17/2020. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review of citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

Most recent electrolytes from the same day are potassium 4.5 mEq/L and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL, both normal. Prescriber review of escitalopram is required.

Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Both are atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the tachycardia needs review.

Persistent atrial fibrillation is documented in every cardiology clinic note from 9/12/2025 through the most recent visit on 6/22/2026. This 80-year-old woman (born 10/26/1945) has no anticoagulant on her current medication list or among her active prescriptions - only aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: age >=75 (2), female (1), hypertension (1), type 2 diabetes (1), congestive heart failure / hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (1), vascular disease - old MI and coronary atherosclerosis (1), and prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria, dysphagia and hemiparesis (2). Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation (class 1) at this risk level; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Anticoagulation needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

Atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 427.31, condition 7010d0e5, 8/22/2025) is an active problem and is restated in the cardiology clinic notes, most recently 6/27/2026. This 71-year-old man (born 8/23/1955) is on no anticoagulant: the current medication list at the last visit was levothyroxine 50 mcg daily only, and the only active prescription is levothyroxine. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (1), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery (1). A score of >=2 in a man carries a class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Note the chart also records hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025), so any decision to withhold anticoagulation should be documented explicitly after review.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0, condition 66dd1300) was diagnosed on 3/14/2025 during an admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism of a cerebral artery - i.e. a cardioembolic stroke. This 71-year-old woman (born 9/7/1955) has no anticoagulant current: her active prescriptions are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: age 65-74 (1), female (1), hypertension (1), prior stroke (2). Anticoagulation is a class 1 recommendation, and is particularly compelling for secondary prevention after an embolic stroke with documented AF. The 3/14/2025 ECG (102298909) showed sinus rhythm with a single ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is listed in the history of every cardiology clinic note from 7/19/2025 to the most recent visit on 8/4/2026, and the chart carries a cardiac dysrhythmia diagnosis (2e31215b) plus a coded history of long-term anticoagulant use. This 48-year-old man (born 2/27/1978) currently takes famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only - no anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: congestive heart failure (acute systolic heart failure / cardiomyopathy documented 2/26/2025, conditions 4f51180a and 1637f513) (1) and hypertension (1). A score of >=2 in a man is a class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so either anticoagulation should be started or the reason for withholding it (and the accuracy of the AF and heart-failure history) should be documented.

ECG of 8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular, with upright P waves in II and a PR of 140 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +58 degrees (normal). QT 318 ms, QTc 413 ms. The prior tracing (102910502) was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 100/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 407 ms), so there are no interval changes.

ECG of 10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), with a low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave in II before every QRS and a PR of 168 ms - no AV block on this tracing despite the coded history of Mobitz II block, and no atrial fibrillation despite the AF history. QRS 88 ms with prominent voltage (V6 R 3.3 mV) but no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 433 ms, Bazett QTc 402 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/22/2023 (104629882: sinus 58/min with one atrial ectopic beat, QTc 371 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

ECG of 12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, extremely regular (RR 492-496 ms), with a small upright P wave in II and a PR of 126 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms. Low-amplitude limb-lead complexes with a net negative QRS in lead I and net positive aVF give a frontal axis of about +143 degrees, i.e. right axis deviation (the axis is close to indeterminate given the small voltages). QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. The prior ECG from the same day at 01:33 (106516875) showed a QRS of 148 ms with a tall terminal R wave in V1 and wide S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - which has resolved on this tracing, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK applies. QTc fell by 55 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

ECG of 11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular (RR 944-982 ms), with a consistent upright P wave in II and a PR of 168 ms. QRS 96 ms - no bundle branch block; axis +67 degrees (normal). QT 550 ms with a Bazett QTc of 559 ms, markedly prolonged. Compared with the prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (108780865: sinus bradycardia 47/min with one atrial ectopic beat, PR 182 ms, QTc 410 ms) the QTc has increased by about 149 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged. Amiodarone was started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit, two weeks before this tracing - see the QT safety review item.

ECG of 9/17/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular with RR intervals from 386 to 1092 ms (coefficient of variation 0.30, RMSSD 264 ms), no organised P waves are seen and the pre-QRS segments do not repeat from beat to beat (beat-to-beat correlation 0.37), so no PR interval is measurable. Mean ventricular rate 99/min. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -53 degrees, left axis deviation. QT 332 ms with a Bazett QTc of 426 ms using the median RR. No prior ECG for comparison; this tracing documents the atrial fibrillation for which the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

This tracing predates the escitalopram started on 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

QT 393 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms - normal. QT 403 ms, Bazett QTc 455 ms - borderline. This 80-year-old woman (born 10/26/1945) has no anticoagulant on her current medication list or among her active prescriptions - only aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: age >=75 (2), female (1), hypertension (1), type 2 diabetes (1), congestive heart failure / hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (1), vascular disease - old MI and coronary atherosclerosis (1), and prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria, dysphagia and hemiparesis (2). Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation (class 1) at this risk level; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Anticoagulation needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: age 65-74 (1), female (1), hypertension (1), prior stroke (2). Both are atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the tachycardia needs review.

Persistent atrial fibrillation is documented in every cardiology clinic note from 9/12/2025 through the most recent visit on 6/22/2026. This 80-year-old woman (born 10/26/1945) has no anticoagulant on her current medication list or among her active prescriptions - only aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: age >=75 (2), female (1), hypertension (1), type 2 diabetes (1), congestive heart failure / hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (1), vascular disease - old MI and coronary atherosclerosis (1), and prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria, dysphagia and hemiparesis (2). Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation (class 1) at this risk level; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Anticoagulation needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

Atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 427.31, condition 7010d0e5, 8/22/2025) is an active problem and is restated in the cardiology clinic notes, most recently 6/27/2026. This 71-year-old man (born 8/23/1955) is on no anticoagulant: the current medication list at the last visit was levothyroxine 50 mcg daily only, and the only active prescription is levothyroxine. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (1), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery (1). A score of >=2 in a man carries a class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Note the chart also records hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025), so any decision to withhold anticoagulation should be documented explicitly after review.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0, condition 66dd1300) was diagnosed on 3/14/2025 during an admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism of a cerebral artery - i.e. a cardioembolic stroke. This 71-year-old woman (born 9/7/1955) has no anticoagulant current: her active prescriptions are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: age 65-74 (1), female (1), hypertension (1), prior stroke (2). Anticoagulation is a class 1 recommendation, and is particularly compelling for secondary prevention after an embolic stroke with documented AF. The 3/14/2025 ECG (102298909) showed sinus rhythm with a single ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is listed in the history of every cardiology clinic note from 7/19/2025 to the most recent visit on 8/4/2026, and the chart carries a cardiac dysrhythmia diagnosis (2e31215b) plus a coded history of long-term anticoagulant use. This 48-year-old man (born 2/27/1978) currently takes famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only - no anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: congestive heart failure (acute systolic heart failure / cardiomyopathy documented 2/26/2025, conditions 4f51180a and 1637f513) (1) and hypertension (1). A score of >=2 in a man is a class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so either anticoagulation should be started or the reason for withholding it (and the accuracy of the AF and heart-failure history) should be documented.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is current (order 438668cc, 7/18/2026 to 12/26/2026; it has been continuously prescribed since 5/14/2024). The most recent ECG, 108018814 of 10/8/2023, shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 503 ms and Bazett QTc 536 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, and 177 ms longer than the QTc of 359 ms on the preceding ECG of 11/23/2022. The 5/14/2024 note that started escitalopram described this ECG as having an acceptable QT, which is not correct. Most recent electrolytes (3/18/2026) are potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL - low-normal, offering no protection. Prescriber review of escitalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, is current (order e78404bf, 7/12/2026 to 1/9/2027; started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit). The most recent ECG, 106885519 of 11/24/2025, shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, PR 168 ms, QRS 96 ms, QT 550 ms and Bazett QTc 559 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold, and 149 ms longer than the QTc of 410 ms on the previous ECG of 6/7/2025 (i.e. after amiodarone was started). Most recent electrolytes (6/9/2026) potassium 4.3 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL are normal, so the prolongation is drug related. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

interpretations.explanation: ECG of 3/7/2026, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of 81/min (RR 656-856 ms, gradual slowing typical of sinus arrhythmia); an upright P wave of about 0.18 mV precedes every QRS in lead II with a constant PR of 184 ms. QRS 76 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +48 degrees (normal). QT 327 ms, Bazett QTc 379 ms - normal despite citalopram 40 mg daily. No prior ECG for comparison. This confirms the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

ECG of 7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 104/min, regular (RR 568-586 ms), upright P waves in II (0.18 mV) with a PR of 128 ms - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal AF is documented in the notes. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +37 degrees (normal). QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 486 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 6/20/2025 (100698634: sinus tachycardia 147/min, PR 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 432 ms) the rate has slowed; the QTc rose by about 54 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold, and rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

ECG of 5/21/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus tachycardia at 110/min, regular (RR 540-614 ms), with upright P waves in II before each QRS and a PR of 118 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 342 ms; Bazett QTc 462 ms, mildly prolonged largely because of rate correction at this heart rate. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 6/10/2026 19:36. Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: mean rate 144/min with irregularly irregular RR intervals from 348 to 650 ms (CV 0.16, RMSSD 98 ms), no consistent P waves (beat-to-beat pre-QRS correlation 0.41) and therefore no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +1 degree (normal). QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 440 ms. The prior tracing from earlier the same day (107914094, 17:13) showed the same rhythm at 139/min with QTc 436 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note recorded this study as normal sinus rhythm at 72/min, which is contradicted by both tracings.

ECG of 8/2/2025. Sinus rhythm at 69/min, very regular (RR 864-884 ms), with repeatable atrial activity before every QRS and a PR of 148 ms. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal, with a leftward tendency: lead I strongly positive, aVL positive, III negative). QT 408 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 (104232242) shows sinus rhythm at 60/min with QTc 408 ms but with reversed arm leads (negative P and QRS in lead I, positive QRS in aVR, normal precordial progression), which accounts for its apparently extreme axis. No change in rhythm or conduction, and the QTc difference of 29 ms is below the 60 ms threshold.

ECG of 5/23/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 596-630 ms), with upright P waves in II (0.17 mV) and a PR of 104 ms. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +4 degrees (normal). QT 306 ms, Bazett QTc 390 ms - normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 12/25/2025, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus rhythm at 72/min, regular (RR 820-840 ms), with a consistent upright P wave in II and a PR of 138 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +22 degrees (normal). QT 381 ms, Bazett QTc 418 ms - normal. No prior ECG for comparison. This tracing predates the escitalopram started on 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

ECG of 11/15/2024. Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response: mean rate 53/min with markedly irregular RR intervals from 694 to 1164 ms (CV 0.20, RMSSD 288 ms), no organised P waves and no reproducible pre-QRS atrial activity (beat-to-beat correlation 0.22), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +27 degrees (normal). QT 461 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms using the median RR. The prior ECG of 11/12/2024 (107873952) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear 0.22 mV P waves, PR 168 ms and QTc 401 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF); the QTc change of about 33 ms is below the 60 ms threshold.

ECG of 3/9/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 58/min, regular (RR 976-1080 ms), with upright P waves in II (0.18 mV) and a PR of 108 ms. QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +61 degrees (normal). QT 393 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms - normal. The prior ECG of 3/8/2025 (106045460: sinus 62/min, PR 110 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 426 ms) is essentially the same; the 39 ms QTc difference is below the 60 ms threshold. This tracing predates the haloperidol started on 9/15/2026.

ECG of 8/23/2025, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus rhythm at 83/min, very regular (RR 716-726 ms), with consistent upright P waves in II and a PR of 144 ms. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +53 degrees (normal). QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 410 ms - normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 6/19/2020. Sinus rhythm at 77/min, regular (RR 774-804 ms), with prominent upright P waves in II (0.24 mV) and a PR of 152 ms. QRS 66 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +64 degrees (normal). QT 403 ms, Bazett QTc 455 ms - borderline. The prior ECG of 2/2/2020 (109048192) also showed a regular sinus rhythm at 75/min with QRS 64 ms but a QTc of about 511 ms on a noisier tracing with inverted T waves; the fall of roughly 56 ms does not reach the 60 ms threshold, and rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

ECG of 1/18/2021. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, very regular (RR 494-504 ms), with consistent upright P waves in II and a PR of 142 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +52 degrees (normal). QT 274 ms, QTc 389 ms (Bazett). Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (106186980: sinus tachycardia 108/min, PR 170 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 396 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc - only a slightly faster rate.

ECG of 6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 54/min, regular (RR 1068-1120 ms), with upright P waves in II and a prolonged PR interval of 212 ms - first degree AV block. QRS 82 ms with a prominent R wave in V1 but no bundle branch block; axis +5 degrees (normal). QT 401 ms, Bazett QTc 382 ms - normal. The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 (103042067) showed sinus bradycardia at 51/min with a PR of 186 ms and QTc 364 ms, so the PR has lengthened slightly into the first degree AV block range; rhythm is unchanged and the QTc change of 18 ms is below the 60 ms threshold (PR prolongation is not one of the listed change categories).

Atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response: mean rate 153/min with irregularly irregular RR intervals from 288 to 580 ms (CV 0.19), no organised P waves and no reproducible pre-QRS atrial activity (beat-to-beat correlation 0.28), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis -11 degrees (normal). QT 264 ms, Bazett QTc 422 ms. The prior ECG of 9/12/2025 (107374881) showed sinus rhythm at 77/min with visible P waves, PR 140 ms and QTc 414 ms (a single atrial ectopic beat and pause), so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF); the QTc change of 8 ms is not significant. Apixaban is current.

ECG of 11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 73/min (RR 788-922 ms) with prominent upright P waves in II (0.20 mV) and a PR of 166 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +12 degrees (normal). QT 359 ms, Bazett QTc 397 ms - normal, consistent with the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm. The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 (105362569) showed sinus rhythm at 67/min with a QT of 505 ms and QTc 534 ms, so the QTc has fallen by about 137 ms and QTC_DECREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

ECG of 10/8/2023. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, regular, with upright P waves in II and a PR of 128 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +47 degrees (normal). The T wave is broad and late: QT 503 ms with a Bazett QTc of 536 ms, markedly prolonged. Compared with the prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (100065910: sinus 75/min, QTc 359 ms) the QTc has risen by about 177 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged. Escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug, is current - see the QT safety review item.

ECG of 4/19/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular (RR 492-500 ms), upright P in II with PR 130 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +68 degrees (normal). QT 284 ms, Bazett QTc 403 ms - normal. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG of 8/23/2021 10:07. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, regular, with upright P waves in II and a PR of 140 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +58 degrees (normal). QT 318 ms, QTc 413 ms. The prior tracing (102910502) was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 100/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 407 ms), so there are no interval changes.

ECG of 10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1144-1178 ms), with a low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave in II before every QRS and a PR of 168 ms - no AV block on this tracing despite the coded history of Mobitz II block, and no atrial fibrillation despite the AF history. QRS 88 ms with prominent voltage (V6 R 3.3 mV) but no bundle branch block; axis +36 degrees (normal). QT 433 ms, Bazett QTc 402 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/22/2023 (104629882: sinus 58/min with one atrial ectopic beat, QTc 371 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

ECG of 12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, extremely regular (RR 492-496 ms), with a small upright P wave in II and a PR of 126 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms. Low-amplitude limb-lead complexes with a net negative QRS in lead I and net positive aVF give a frontal axis of about +143 degrees, i.e. right axis deviation (the axis is close to indeterminate given the small voltages). QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 419 ms. The prior ECG from the same day at 01:33 (106516875) showed a QRS of 148 ms with a tall terminal R wave in V1 and wide S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - which has resolved on this tracing, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK applies. QTc fell by 55 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

ECG of 11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62/min, regular (RR 944-982 ms), with a consistent upright P wave in II and a PR of 168 ms. QRS 96 ms - no bundle branch block; axis +67 degrees (normal). QT 550 ms with a Bazett QTc of 559 ms, markedly prolonged. Compared with the prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (108780865: sinus bradycardia 47/min with one atrial ectopic beat, PR 182 ms, QTc 410 ms) the QTc has increased by about 149 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 applies; rhythm and conduction are unchanged. Amiodarone was started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit, two weeks before this tracing - see the QT safety review item.

ECG of 9/17/2024, the only tracing for this patient. Atrial fibrillation: the rhythm is irregularly irregular with RR intervals from 386 to 1092 ms (coefficient of variation 0.30, RMSSD 264 ms), no organised P waves are seen and the pre-QRS segments do not repeat from beat to beat (beat-to-beat correlation 0.37), so no PR interval is measurable. Mean ventricular rate 99/min. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -53 degrees, left axis deviation. QT 332 ms with a Bazett QTc of 426 ms using the median RR. No prior ECG for comparison; this tracing documents the atrial fibrillation for which the patient is anticoagulated with warfarin.

items.explanation: Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban, but both prescriptions were written that day and both remain current at 9/24/2026: rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order c4b6df94, valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7c496afb, valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026). The visit note lists both on the current medication list. Concurrent DOAC therapy markedly increases bleeding risk (this patient also takes clopidogrel) and the rivaroxaban order should be discontinued.

Citalopram 40 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is current (order 62da0901, 7/15/2026 to 1/7/2027; continuously prescribed since 10/2/2023). The dose also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised for patients over 60. The most recent ECG, 104821039 of 11/10/2023, shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 505 ms and Bazett QTc 545 ms, above the 500 ms threshold and 101 ms longer than the QTc of 444 ms on the prior ECG of 6/17/2020. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review of citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, is current (order 018076d6, 5/30/2026 to 1/10/2027; started at the 2/12/2026 cardiology clinic visit). The only and most recent ECG, 101538691 of 3/8/2026 - obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started - shows sinus rhythm at 68/min, PR 140 ms, QRS 80 ms, QT 503 ms and Bazett QTc 536 ms, above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent electrolytes from the same day are potassium 4.5 mEq/L and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL, both normal. Prescriber review of escitalopram is required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, is current (order c67148bf, 6/17/2026 to 1/6/2027; on the medication list continuously since 3/1/2022). The most recent ECG, 101515306 of 4/27/2022, shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with PR 198 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 578 ms and Bazett QTc 567 ms - far above the 500 ms threshold, and 132 ms longer than the QTc of 435 ms on the prior ECG of 4/6/2022. This 95-year-old woman is also on warfarin and metoprolol. Most recent electrolytes (6/17/2026) are potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025 (order 5d345f42; amiodarone was absent from the medication list at the preceding 9/21/2025 visit). The start is on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 559 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026 (order 0d807827, written at that visit and the first outpatient escitalopram order for this patient). Because the start was before 3/1/2026 the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies, so an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start - within the window, so the requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 536 ms - see the separate QT safety item.)

Citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026 (order 6f20ee78; citalopram was not on the medication list at the 12/15/2025 visit). The start is on or after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met (sinus rhythm, QTc 379 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026 (order ead8699a, the first escitalopram order for this patient). The start is on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was not recorded until 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start and 5 days after the deadline - so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue as of 9/24/2026. Escitalopram has been continued (current order b9bce5cd).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (order 9fa1dfe1; escitalopram was not on the medication list at the previous visit on 2/18/2026). The start is on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been recorded since the start - the only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 12/25/2025 - and no outside ECG is referenced, so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026 (order d7292a2a; escitalopram was not on the medication list at any previous visit, most recently 3/8/2026). The start is on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 (5e12a8aa) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the required window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. If that tracing is obtained it would satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined from the chart; the outside report needs to be chased.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily, a QT watch-list medication, was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026 (order 34d26a30; haloperidol was not on the outpatient medication list at any earlier visit). The start is on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is due within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the most recent tracings are 106045460 and 104253928 from March 2025), but the deadline falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is current (order a0184d35, written 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027). Outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Apixaban was nevertheless re-listed and re-prescribed at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit, together with aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg (triple antithrombotic therapy), without any documented decision on resuming anticoagulation after the bleed. The indication is atrial flutter; benefit/risk of resuming apixaban (and of concurrent aspirin plus clopidogrel) needs prescriber review.

Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026 (observation 4282f19b), 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

The anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 documents a home INR of 3.4 and a warfarin decrease from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the clinic protocol - a dose change by a clinic pharmacist, which the 3/1/2026 memo covers. A follow-up INR was therefore required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since the change (the last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; the 3.4 value is the pre-change home reading that prompted it), so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation (class 1) at this risk level; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Anticoagulation needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

Atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 427.31, condition 7010d0e5, 8/22/2025) is an active problem and is restated in the cardiology clinic notes, most recently 6/27/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (1), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery (1). A score of >=2 in a man carries a class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Note the chart also records hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025), so any decision to withhold anticoagulation should be documented explicitly after review.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0, condition 66dd1300) was diagnosed on 3/14/2025 during an admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism of a cerebral artery - i.e. a cardioembolic stroke. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: age 65-74 (1), female (1), hypertension (1), prior stroke (2). Anticoagulation is a class 1 recommendation, and is particularly compelling for secondary prevention after an embolic stroke with documented AF. The 3/14/2025 ECG (102298909) showed sinus rhythm with a single ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

A score of >=2 in a man is a class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so either anticoagulation should be started or the reason for withholding it (and the accuracy of the AF and heart-failure history) should be documented.

items.explanation: Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active. The visit note lists both on the current medication list. Concurrent DOAC therapy markedly increases bleeding risk (this patient also takes clopidogrel) and the rivaroxaban order should be discontinued.

Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Prescriber review of citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

This 80-year-old woman (born 10/26/1945) has no anticoagulant on her current medication list or among her active prescriptions - only aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: age >=75 (2), female (1), hypertension (1), type 2 diabetes (1), congestive heart failure / hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (1), vascular disease - old MI and coronary atherosclerosis (1), and prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria, dysphagia and hemiparesis (2). Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation (class 1) at this risk level; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Anticoagulation needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

Atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 427.31, condition 7010d0e5, 8/22/2025) is an active problem and is restated in the cardiology clinic notes, most recently 6/27/2026. A score of >=2 in a man carries a class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Note the chart also records hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025), so any decision to withhold anticoagulation should be documented explicitly after review.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0, condition 66dd1300) was diagnosed on 3/14/2025 during an admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism of a cerebral artery - i.e. a cardioembolic stroke. This 71-year-old woman (born 9/7/1955) has no anticoagulant current: her active prescriptions are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: age 65-74 (1), female (1), hypertension (1), prior stroke (2). Anticoagulation is a class 1 recommendation, and is particularly compelling for secondary prevention after an embolic stroke with documented AF. The 3/14/2025 ECG (102298909) showed sinus rhythm with a single ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is listed in the history of every cardiology clinic note from 7/19/2025 to the most recent visit on 8/4/2026, and the chart carries a cardiac dysrhythmia diagnosis (2e31215b) plus a coded history of long-term anticoagulant use. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: congestive heart failure (acute systolic heart failure / cardiomyopathy documented 2/26/2025, conditions 4f51180a and 1637f513) (1) and hypertension (1). A score of >=2 in a man is a class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so either anticoagulation should be started or the reason for withholding it (and the accuracy of the AF and heart-failure history) should be documented.

Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation (class 1) at this risk level; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Anticoagulation needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

A score of >=2 in a man carries a class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Note the chart also records hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025), so any decision to withhold anticoagulation should be documented explicitly after review.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: age 65-74 (1), female (1), hypertension (1), prior stroke (2). Anticoagulation is a class 1 recommendation, and is particularly compelling for secondary prevention after an embolic stroke with documented AF. The 3/14/2025 ECG (102298909) showed sinus rhythm with a single ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

A follow-up INR was therefore required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since the change (the last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; the 3.4 value is the pre-change home reading that prompted it), so the requirement is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (6/10/2026 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of 139/min with no consistent P waves, and 103088543 (6/10/2026 19:36) shows the same pattern at 144/min (RR intervals 348-650 ms, beat-to-beat P-wave correlation 0.41). Both are atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. The documented rhythm and rate need correction and the tachycardia needs review.

Persistent atrial fibrillation is documented in every cardiology clinic note from 9/12/2025 through the most recent visit on 6/22/2026. This 80-year-old woman (born 10/26/1945) has no anticoagulant on her current medication list or among her active prescriptions - only aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: age >=75 (2), female (1), hypertension (1), type 2 diabetes (1), congestive heart failure / hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (1), vascular disease - old MI and coronary atherosclerosis (1), and prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria, dysphagia and hemiparesis (2). Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation (class 1) at this risk level; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Anticoagulation needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

Atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 427.31, condition 7010d0e5, 8/22/2025) is an active problem and is restated in the cardiology clinic notes, most recently 6/27/2026. This 71-year-old man (born 8/23/1955) is on no anticoagulant: the current medication list at the last visit was levothyroxine 50 mcg daily only, and the only active prescription is levothyroxine. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension (1), age 65-74 (1), vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery (1). A score of >=2 in a man carries a class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation. Note the chart also records hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025), so any decision to withhold anticoagulation should be documented explicitly after review.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.0, condition 66dd1300) was diagnosed on 3/14/2025 during an admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism of a cerebral artery - i.e. a cardioembolic stroke. This 71-year-old woman (born 9/7/1955) has no anticoagulant current: her active prescriptions are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine only. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: age 65-74 (1), female (1), hypertension (1), prior stroke (2). Anticoagulation is a class 1 recommendation, and is particularly compelling for secondary prevention after an embolic stroke with documented AF. The 3/14/2025 ECG (102298909) showed sinus rhythm with a single ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is listed in the history of every cardiology clinic note from 7/19/2025 to the most recent visit on 8/4/2026, and the chart carries a cardiac dysrhythmia diagnosis (2e31215b) plus a coded history of long-term anticoagulant use. Guidelines recommend oral anticoagulation (class 1) at this risk level; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Anticoagulation needs to be started or an explicit contraindication documented.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: age 65-74 (1), female (1), hypertension (1), prior stroke (2). Anticoagulation is a class 1 recommendation, and is particularly compelling for secondary prevention after an embolic stroke with documented AF. The 3/14/2025 ECG (102298909) showed sinus rhythm with a single ectopic beat, which does not exclude paroxysmal AF.
